description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. description: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Chemical Biological Center (DEVCOM CBC), Rock Island, IL, on behalf of the Office of the Secretary of Defense, Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Industrial Base Policy Innovation Capability and Modernization office via its Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment (IBAS) Program (10 U.S.C. � 4817), in conjunction with Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI), manages the Cornerstone Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022. Cornerstone was architected to create a broad-based, flexible and enduring public-private consortium focused on strategic strengthening of the U.S. Manufacturing and Defense Industrial Base and provide a strong complement to the mandates in Presidential Executive Order 13806. ACC-RI, on behalf of DEVCOM CBC, intends to issue a competitive Cornerstone Initiative Request (CIR) for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology on or after 08 October 2026, with an estimated closing date of 30 calendar days after issuance. The CIR for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology is restricted to Cornerstone consortium members. The CIR will solicit proposals for (1) fixed-price OTA with incremental payments made upon completion of specific milestones. Period of performance will be 36 months. A non-competitive follow-on production OT may be awarded following a successful prototype. The objective of this other transaction prototype project is to design, develop, and demonstrate the Generation 2 (Gen 2) Continuous Feed Narcotics Destruction prototype to modernize and streamline the disposal of seized illicit substances. This effort directly addresses critical logistical bottlenecks, high-maintenance footprints, and security vulnerabilities inherent in legacy batch-feed disposal systems. By transitioning to a high-throughput, continuous-feed technological architecture, this prototype accelerates destruction cycle times, significantly reducing the security risks, costs, and logistical burdens associated with the long-term storage and nationwide transport of seized contraband. Subject to funding, The Cornerstone CIR will solicit prototype fixed-priced proposals for two one Expenditure OTA Agreements with incremental payments made upon completion of specific milestones. The period of performance is estimated to be 36 months. A non-competitive follow-on production OT may be awarded following a successful prototype. Any OT awarded as a result of this initiative will incorporate the following clauses: 1. FAR clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment 2. DFARS clause 252.232-7006, WAWF Payment Instructions 3. DFARS clause 252.204-7012, Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting. The CIR is restricted to Cornerstone Consortium members only and will be communicated to the Cornerstone Consortium and companies with pending applications via email. Entities are required to have begun the membership process for their proposal to be reviewed. Entities must have an active registration in SAM.gov, a favorable status in Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information Systems, and be members of the Cornerstone Consortium, with a signed Cornerstone Consortium Management Agreement, to be eligible to submit a proposal and be eligible for awarded this of an OTA task. Contractors may obtain Cornerstone registration information located at https://cornerstone.army.mil or by inquiring at: usarmy.ria.devcom-cbc.mbx.cornerstone-ota@army.mil. title: USCG - Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. Phase II - Each Phase I IDIQ awardee will be issued an initial delivery order satisfying the minimum guarantee under its IDIQ contract to complete the detailed construction/production design, build one (1) demonstration vessel, and participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration. The Government will evaluate the results of each demonstration vessel in accordance with the Phase II evaluation methodology established in the solicitation. Following completion of the Phase II evaluation, the Government anticipates selecting one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive subsequent RB-S III production orders during the remaining ordering period. The final ordering structure and procedures will be established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated solicitation will provide the specific Phase I and Phase II evaluation criteria, evaluation methodology, and basis for selecting the IDIQ contractor anticipated to receive subsequent production orders. title: USCG - Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. Phase II - Each Phase I IDIQ awardee will be issued an initial delivery order satisfying the minimum guarantee under its IDIQ contract to complete the detailed construction/production design, build one (1) demonstration vessel, and participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration. The Government will evaluate the results of each demonstration vessel in accordance with the Phase II evaluation methodology established in the solicitation. Following completion of the Phase II evaluation, the Government anticipates selecting one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive subsequent RB-S III production orders during the remaining ordering period. The final ordering structure and procedures will be established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated solicitation will provide the specific Phase I and Phase II evaluation criteria, evaluation methodology, and basis for selecting the IDIQ contractor anticipated to receive subsequent production orders. title: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has made a direct award of an definitized single award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract number 693KA8-26-D-00018 to Frequentis USA, Inc, for Digital Remote Towers. This award was made using t
description: Section 161 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018 laid the groundwork for the development and implementation of remote tower systems (RTSs) to support the modernization of air traffic control services. This initiative aims to explore and deploy RT technology as a cost-effective and efficient alternative to traditional air traffic control towers (ATCTs), particularly in rural and small community airports. The RT program is designed to enhance the FAA's ability to integrate innovative technologies into the National Airspace System (NAS) while maintaining the highest standards of safety and efficiency. RTs provide Visual Flight Rules (VFR) services that extend air traffic control capabilities to underserved areas. The RT program supports the modernization of ATCT infrastructures and promotes cost efficient tower solutions at VFR airports within the (NAS). The program facilitates the evaluation and deployment of RTs, ensuring that they seamlessly transition into real-world operational environments. This initiative supports the FAA's mission to modernize air traffic management and maintain safety and efficiency across the NAS. Under FAA direction and safety oversight, selected airports will integrate and operationalize RT technology, leveraging the insights gained from the System Design Approval (SDA) at the Tech Center. Additional research goals and objectives for government-funded activities may be outlined for sites in specific tasks under the IDIQ. This will help the government evaluate and improve RT technologies in its efforts to continually improve the safety and efficiency of the NAS. This will support the collection and analysis of data essential for: 1. Optimizing RT operations within a multi-runway operational environment. 2. Evaluating the performance and reliability of remote sensing and communication technologies under varied operational conditions. 3. Assessing the infrastructure requirements and scalability of RTS in broader deployment and diverse airport settings. 4. Collecting operational data to inform future policy, safety approvals and implementation decisions. Justification for a Direct Award is summarized as follows: Frequentis (FRQ) is an established global provider of air traffic management and RT solutions. FRQ has deployed digital tower systems internationally and specializes in mission-critical communication and control systems for aviation environments. FRQ has worked in coordination with the FAA and the William J. Hughes Technical Center to develop, and configure, a RTS aligned with FAA safety, human factors, and operational requirements. The FRQ RTS is the only solution that has progressed through the FAA�s SDA process to date. While other vendors offer RT technologies globally, no other system has achieved comparable advancement within the FAA�s design approval and integration framework. Selecting an alternative vendor at this stage would require duplicative design approval activities, additional technical evaluation, and extended safety validation, resulting in significant schedule delays and increased program costs. The program�s reason to establish the RT Program is to comply with Section 621 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024, which mandates the development and deployment of RT technologies. This initiative aims to enhance air traffic management capabilities at rural and small community airports by integrating advanced RTSs into the NAS. The program is also supporting FAA strategic objectives to modernize the NAS through implementation of innovative, scalable, and cost-effective technologies. RTSs provide a viable alternative to traditional air traffic control infrastructure, enabling expanded service capabilities while optimizing resource utilization across a diverse range of airport environments. Currently, FRQ is the only vendor with a technically acceptable system to comply with the Reauthorization Act of 2024. To meet the requirements, the FAA must leverage the only system that has achieved the necessary level of technical maturity and alignment with FAA standards. While the FAA is actively conducting outreach to additional vendors to participate in the SDA process, onboarding and evaluating alternative systems will require additional time for design approval, testing and validation, and will not support immediate program timelines.

CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. description: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Chemical Biological Center (DEVCOM CBC), Rock Island, IL, on behalf of the Office of the Secretary of Defense, Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Industrial Base Policy Innovation Capability and Modernization office via its Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment (IBAS) Program (10 U.S.C. � 4817), in conjunction with Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI), manages the Cornerstone Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022. Cornerstone was architected to create a broad-based, flexible and enduring public-private consortium focused on strategic strengthening of the U.S. Manufacturing and Defense Industrial Base and provide a strong complement to the mandates in Presidential Executive Order 13806. ACC-RI, on behalf of DEVCOM CBC, intends to issue a competitive Cornerstone Initiative Request (CIR) for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology on or after 08 October 2026, with an estimated closing date of 30 calendar days after issuance. The CIR for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology is restricted to Cornerstone consortium members. The CIR will solicit white paper proposals for (1) fixed-price OTA with incremental payments made upon completion of specific milestones. Period of performance will be 36 months. A non-competitive follow-on production OT may be awarded following a successful prototype. The objective of this other transaction prototype project is to design, develop, and demonstrate the Generation 2 (Gen 2) Continuous Feed Narcotics Destruction prototype to modernize and streamline the disposal of seized illicit substances. This effort directly addresses critical logistical bottlenecks, high-maintenance footprints, and security vulnerabilities inherent in legacy batch-feed disposal systems. By transitioning to a high-throughput, continuous-feed technological architecture, this prototype accelerates destruction cycle times, significantly reducing the security risks, costs, and logistical burdens associated with the long-term storage and nationwide transport of seized contraband. Any OT awarded as a result of this initiative will incorporate the following clauses: 1. FAR clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment 2. DFARS clause 252.232-7006, WAWF Payment Instructions 3. DFARS clause 252.204-7012, Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting. The CIR is restricted to Cornerstone Consortium members only and will be communicated to the Cornerstone Consortium and companies with pending applications via email. Entities are required to have begun the membership process for their proposal to be reviewed. Entities must have an active registration in SAM.gov, a favorable status in Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information Systems, and be members of the Cornerstone Consortium, with a signed Cornerstone Consortium Management Agreement, to be eligible to submit a proposal and be eligible for awarded this of an OTA task. description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. Phase II - Each Phase I IDIQ awardee will be issued an initial delivery order satisfying the minimum guarantee under its IDIQ contract to complete the detailed construction/production design, build one (1) demonstration vessel, and participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration. The Government will evaluate the results of each demonstration vessel in accordance with the Phase II evaluation methodology established in the solicitation. Following completion of the Phase II evaluation, the Government anticipates selecting one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive subsequent RB-S III production orders during the remaining ordering period. The final ordering structure and procedures will be established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated solicitation will provide the specific Phase I and Phase II evaluation criteria, evaluation methodology, and basis for selecting the IDIQ contractor anticipated to receive subsequent production orders. description: The primary objective of this work under Solicitation Number N3943026R5001 is to establish a scientifically sound methodology to quantify and evaluate per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) distributions in precipitation, ambient fog water, and ambient soils at multiple active U.S. Navy installations. description: This is a pre-solicitation notice and not a request for proposals. As such, vendors are not to send capability statements or other such documents. Summary: This project includes building the SMTF at the James J. Rowley Training Center (JJRTC), which is the primary training facility for the United States Secret Service (USSS). The training center consists of multiple buildings and structures that provide an environment for various training activities, including active scenario training, as well as classroom and conference room space. Due to increased operational tempo, development of new training programs, and campus population growth in recent years, the USSS continues to develop the JJRTC campus to meet the needs of the USSS mission. To enhance training activities and operational readiness, the USSS intends to construct a full-scale site and building representation of the White House, perimeter buildings, and grounds. Project Scope: The project consists of the work associated with the Site, Center Building, and Perimeter Buildings as described below: Site: The general scope of the project is to replicate (or match) the original building�s grounds on the proposed JJRTC project site. This includes matching both the horizontal and vertical site features of the original grounds. The limits of this replica are the outer curb lines of the proposed perimeter roads (Pennsylvania Avenue, E Street, and West/East Executive Avenue). The scope includes providing stormwater management based on the Maryland Department of the Environment�s (MDE�s) requirements. In addition, existing utilities serving the JJRTC facility will be improved and extended to service the project site. As extensive re-grading will be required, most of the flora and fauna will need to be removed from the site. The proposed replacement flora will include inexpensive, fast-growing, and low-maintenance species. Trees will be matched by general size and either evergreen or deciduous. These types should be selected and placed to match the visual and security functions of the existing trees in the original landscape. Deciduous trees should include shade trees and ornamental (flowering trees). Building interiors support multiple training and training support functions. Major building floor areas mirror the original building floor layout, however selected areas designated for dynamic training will be a replica of the original building�s interior conditions without attempting historic and decorative reproduction. Notre philosophie d’intervention s’inscrit dans une volonté de préserver ces différentes strates successives comme témoignage à la fois historique et archéologique de l’évolution du bâti. Nous opterons pour une restauration respectueuse des matériaux et de la morphologie actuelle de l’édifice avec ses irrégularités et ses variations. Une attention spécifique sera portée aux ouvrages anciens, à leur typologie, à leurs caractéristiques, à leur identité afin de proposer des interventions les valorisant pour les générations futures. Plus précisément, quatre critères cadrent notre philosophie de restauration et de rénovation pour la Basilique. Ces critères servent de fils conducteur pour déterminer les options d’intervention sur les divers ouvrages. Pour chaque nouvelle option à prendre, nous vérifierons qu’elle se situe dans la continuité de cette philosophie de manière à atteindre une unité dans les interventions à prévoir. Les quatre critères pour la Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre sont les suivants :  La préservation/sauvegarde de l’édifice dans son état actuel (pas de retour vers un état antérieur, pas de démolitions), préservation des matériaux et du mode constructif, sauvegarde des différentes strates/couches archéologiques ;  La pérennité/stabilité des interventions proposées par une remise en état des ouvrages selon la situation actuelle et si nécessaire, la mise en œuvre de protections ou d’améliorations contemporaines spécifiques en vue de créer les conditions optimales de préservation et de durabilité et ce, dans le respect des valeurs patrimoniales des éléments constitutifs ;  L’optimisation des coûts en intervenant sur les questions prioritaires pouvant avoir un impact sur la pérennité/conservation des ouvrages mais sans reconstituer les éléments disparus ou n’ayant qu’un intérêt purement esthétique ;  La garantie de pouvoir utiliser le bâtiment selon son usage actuel et de façon optimale. La proposition s’oriente donc vers une « Restauration-conservatoire » dans le sens où nous cherchons à restaurer les propriétés structurelles et fonctionnelles (d’un ouvrage, des matériaux) nécessaires à la conservation durable/pérenne du bâtiment. La restauration des propriétés structurelles et fonctionnelles d’un ouvrage ou des matériaux se fait soit par remplacement/réparation/consolidation, soit par la mise en place d’une protection.

description: Les présents travaux portent sur la restauration de l’enveloppe extérieure ainsi que sur l’intérieur de la Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre. L’objectif de cette restauration est d’assurer la pérennité de l’édifice tout en conservant ses caractéristiques actuelles et ses différentes strates archéologiques. Les travaux comprennent également la rationalisation et la mise aux normes des installations techniques afin que la Basilique puisse continuer à être utilisée comme lieu de culte. Le marché est divisé en deux lots : > Lot 1 - Restauration de l'enveloppe extérieure et intérieure : Ce lot comprend l'installation de chantier générale, les toitures, façades, menuiseries extérieures et les travaux intérieurs > Lot 2 - Restauration des vitraux : Ce lot comprend toutes les interventions propres aux vitraux La Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre est classée comme Monument suivant l'arrêté royal du 08/03/1938. Philosophie d’intervention : La Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre telle que nous l’observons aujourd’hui est le résultat de modifications et d’agrandissements s’étalant sur huit siècles consécutifs avec une dernière transformation majeure au 18ème siècle réalisée vraisemblablement par l’architecte de la cour Guillaume De Bruyne. Cette dernière transformation a changé irrévocablement la morphologie de l’édifice de telle sorte qu’il n’est plus possible de revenir à une situation antérieure. Les travaux exécutés au 18ème siècle ont été marqués par une volonté d’uniformisation de l’église avec le souhait d’une plus grande harmonie dans la lecture de l’édifice de manière à le voir comme un ensemble et non plus comme l’adjonction d’éléments de différentes époques (construction du collatéral sud sur base du collatéral nord, façade ouest travaillée symétriquement, etc.). L’édifice conserve toutefois dans ses maçonneries, les traces subtiles de son évolution au cours des siècles comme autant de strates successives. Chaque rénovation/transformation a ajouté une nouvelle couche avec les moyens et le style de son époque. Notre philosophie d’intervention s’inscrit dans une volonté de préserver ces différentes strates successives comme témoignage à la fois historique et archéologique de l’évolution du bâti. Nous opterons pour une restauration respectueuse des matériaux et de la morphologie actuelle de l’édifice avec ses irrégularités et ses variations. Une attention spécifique sera portée aux ouvrages anciens, à leur typologie, à leurs caractéristiques, à leur identité afin de proposer des interventions les valorisant pour les générations futures. Plus précisément, quatre critères cadrent notre philosophie de restauration et de rénovation pour la Basilique. Ces critères servent de fils conducteur pour déterminer les options d’intervention sur les divers ouvrages. Pour chaque nouvelle option à prendre, nous vérifierons qu’elle se situe dans la continuité de cette philosophie de manière à atteindre une unité dans les interventions à prévoir. Les quatre critères pour la Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre sont les suivants :  La préservation/sauvegarde de l’édifice dans son état actuel (pas de retour vers un état antérieur, pas de démolitions), préservation des matériaux et du mode constructif, sauvegarde des différentes strates/couches archéologiques ;  La pérennité/stabilité des interventions proposées par une remise en état des ouvrages selon la situation actuelle et si nécessaire, la mise en œuvre de protections ou d’améliorations contemporaines spécifiques en vue de créer les conditions optimales de préservation et de durabilité et ce, dans le respect des valeurs patrimoniales des éléments constitutifs ;  L’optimisation des coûts en intervenant sur les questions prioritaires pouvant avoir un impact sur la pérennité/conservation des ouvrages mais sans reconstituer les éléments disparus ou n’ayant qu’un intérêt purement esthétique ;  La garantie de pouvoir utiliser le bâtiment selon son usage actuel et de façon optimale. La proposition s’oriente donc vers une « Restauration-conservatoire » dans le sens où nous cherchons à restaurer les propriétés structurelles et fonctionnelles (d’un ouvrage, des matériaux) nécessaires à la conservation durable/pérenne du bâtiment. La restauration des propriétés structurelles et fonctionnelles d’un ouvrage ou des matériaux se fait soit par remplacement/réparation/consolidation, soit par la mise en place d’une protection.
